insight.title: Why You Say Yes to Favors You Don’t Want to Do
insight.subtitle: How to stop filling your future schedule with tasks you’ll regret.

sections.text: We often agree to a commitment for next week that we would reject if it were happening in ten minutes. We treat our future time as if it were an infinite, free resource.
Your brain views your "future self" as a stranger. Since you don’t feel the immediate stress of the task, you prioritize short-term social ease over the reality of your actual workload and energy.
This habit creates a calendar full of obligations you never truly wanted. You trade your long-term focus for a fleeting moment of politeness, leaving your future self to pay for your past decisions.
The next time you receive a request today, ask if you would say yes for this afternoon.

news.title: Iran has lost track of mines it planted in Hormuz, reopening delayed: Report
news.description: US officials said that Iran's inability to locate and remove mines it deployed is delaying safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, even as pressure mounts to restore normal shipping traffic.
news.why: Stalled shipping routes will slow down the delivery of your online orders.

news.title: Disney Axes Jobs Again: 1,000 Roles at Risk Amid Major Restructuring
news.description: Disney is reportedly set to lay off nearly 1,000 employees as part of ongoing cost-cutting efforts under new CEO Josh D’Amaro. The job cuts are expected to impact marketing teams amid restructuring, while the company continues investing in digital growth and theme park expansion.
news.why: Finding media work is harder as Disney cuts another 1,000 jobs.

news.title: Autism breakthrough as scientists find 44-cent pill that 'reverses' symptoms
news.description: Researchers at Yale University say they have found a 44-cent-a-pill drug that could treat autistic behaviors, and it's already been approved by the FDA for other health conditions.
news.why: This 44-cent pill could lower your costs for managing autism symptoms.
